THE BOOK OF WAR — COMPLETE TEXT

FRAGMENT 1 — THE PRINCE OF THE CONGREGATION — 4Q285 Fragment 5

1 [As it is written in the book of Yeshayahu the prophet:] The thickets of the forest will be cut down with iron, and the Lebanon will fall by a mighty one. And a shoot will come out from the stump of Yishai and a branch from his roots will bear fruit.

2 The Prince of the Congregation — the Nasi ha-Edah — will stand up against the Kittim. And he will thrust the enemy before him with the sword and drive out all the Kittim from the boundary of Yisra'el.

3 And the priests shall blow the trumpets of alarm and all the men of war shall line up for battle and the sons of Levi shall carry the banner of YHWH before the ranks. And the angels of His holy ones are with them in the battle.

4 And the Prince of the Congregation will judge the nations. He will gather the remnant of Yisra'el from among the peoples and will set them in their tribal portions and will rebuild the ruined cities and establish justice in the gate.

5 For the victory belongs to YHWH alone and the glory of the battle is His. The arm of flesh will not prevail in that day but the arm of The Creator will deliver. Those who trust in weapons will fall but those who trust in YHWH will stand.

6 And in that day there will be no more war in all the land of Yisra'el. The weapons of war will be given to the craftsmen and made into tools of peace. And the children of Yisra'el will dwell in safety from that day until the age to come.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 4Q285 Fragment 5 is the famous "pierced messiah" fragment that caused significant controversy when first published in 1991 because of a misreading. John Strugnell's initial reading suggested the Prince of the Congregation was killed. The correct reading, confirmed by subsequent scholarship, is that the Prince kills the leader of the Kittim. The Prince of the Congregation in this text is a victorious military figure, not a dying saviour.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez prophetic tradition does not contain a direct parallel to this specific text. However the image of a righteous leader from the Davidic line who defeats the enemies of Yisra'el and restores the tribal portions is consistent with the prophetic theology of the Ge'ez Yeshayahu tradition. The restoration of tribal geography is a consistent feature of ancient Afro-Asiatic covenantal eschatology.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Yeshayahu 10:34-11:1 contains the shoot from the stump of Yishai prophecy quoted in this fragment. The Book of War applies this prophecy to a specific eschatological military figure — the Prince of the Congregation — who leads the final battle against the Kittim (Romans). This is a specifically Qumran interpretation of the Yeshayahu text within their eschatological military theology.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The correct reading of Fragment 5 — the Prince kills the Kittim leader rather than being killed — is crucial and must be stated plainly. The initial misreading was not corrected quickly enough in public scholarship, allowing the "pierced messiah" interpretation to circulate and be used to argue for DSS precedents for the Christian crucifixion narrative. The text in fact presents the precise opposite: the anointed military leader of Yisra'el is victorious, not sacrificed.

FRAGMENT 2 — THE BLESSINGS OF VICTORY — 11Q14 Columns 1-2

1 [Blessed be The Creator who teaches the hands of His people for war and the fingers of His holy ones for battle. He will crush the nations before them and tread down the peoples under their feet.]

2 Blessed be the Prince of the Congregation who stands in the day of battle. May YHWH strengthen his hand and give him victory over all his enemies. May the nations tremble before him and may their kings bring tribute to his feet.

3 And the priests shall bless all the men of the covenant and say: Blessed are you in all your going out and in all your coming in. YHWH your Creator goes before you in battle and His angels march at your side.

4 Fear no one. Do not be dismayed before the face of the enemy. For YHWH your Creator is with you and He is greater than all who come against you. His right hand will fight for you and His arm will deliver you.

5 And when the victory is given, offer the first fruits of the battle to YHWH before you take anything for yourselves. For the victory is His and the glory belongs to Him. Let no man take credit for what The Creator has done.

6 And they sang a song of praise to YHWH saying: Great is Your faithfulness, YHWH. You have kept Your covenant with the sons of Avraham, Yitzhak, and Yaakov and You have given us victory over our enemies as You promised. Praise be to Your name forever.

COMPARATIVE MANUSCRIPT NOTES

[DSS] 11Q14 parallels portions of the War Scroll (1QM) and supplements them with additional blessing material. The liturgical format — priestly blessings pronounced over the warriors before and after battle — confirms that the eschatological war of the Qumran community was understood as a sacred ritual event as much as a military one. The boundary between liturgy and warfare dissolves in this theology.

[ORIT GE'EZ] The Orit Ge'ez tradition in the Chanokh corpus describes the final angelic war in cosmic terms. The Book of War presents the earthly counterpart: the human community of the covenant fighting in coordination with the angelic host. Both texts operate within the same ancient Afro-Asiatic understanding that earthly events have exact heavenly counterparts.

[MASORETIC VARIANT] The Masoretic Tehillim contains numerous battle psalms in which YHWH fights for Yisra'el. The Book of War liturgies develop this psalmic tradition into a detailed battle theology with specific roles for priests, trumpets, banners, and angelic accompaniment. The Qumran community systematized what the Masoretic Psalms express in individual lyric form.

[CRITICAL NOTE] The instruction to offer the first fruits of battle to YHWH before taking anything for the warriors is a direct application of agricultural first-fruits theology to warfare. This integration — all domains of life governed by the same covenant obligations — is characteristic of the Qumran community's comprehensive theology. Nothing is secular. Every domain of human action is a covenant obligation or violation.
